question: Calculate the gravitational force between two masses of 5 kg each placed 2 m apart.
gold_answer:
# Solved Numerical

---

## Gravitational Field Problem

### Problem
Calculate the gravitational force between two identical masses of $5 \text{ kg}$ each placed at a center-to-center distance of $2 \text{ m}$ apart.

### Given
* First mass ($m_1$) = $5 \text{ kg}$
* Second mass ($m_2$) = $5 \text{ kg}$
* Distance apart ($r$) = $2 \text{ m}$
* Gravitational Constant ($G$) = $6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$

### Formula
$$F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$$

### Substitution
$$F = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) \times \frac{5 \times 5}{2^2}$$

### Calculation
$$F = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) \times \frac{25}{4}$$

$$F = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) \times 6.25$$

$$F = 4.16875 \times 10^{-10} \text{ N}$$

### Final Answer
**Gravitational Force ($F$) = $4.17 \times 10^{-10} \text{ N}$**

### Interpretation
This reflects an incredibly weak mutual attraction force, demonstrating why gravity is imperceptible between everyday objects and only becomes significant with planetary-scale masses.

## Gravitational Force Between Two Masses
📖 Quick Definition
Every object with mass attracts every other object with mass. This attraction is called gravitational force. The strength of this force depends on how massive the objects are and how far apart they are.
⚡ Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
$$F = \frac{G \cdot m_1 \cdot m_2}{r^2}$$
FGravitational force between the two masses (Newtons, N)
GUniversal gravitational constant = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²
m₁, m₂Masses of the two objects (kg)
rDistance between the centres of the two masses (m)
📋 Given Values
m₁5 kg
m₂5 kg
r2 m
G6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²
🔢 Step-by-Step Solution
Step 1
Write the formula
$$F = \frac{G \cdot m_1 \cdot m_2}{r^2}$$
Step 2
Substitute the values
$$F = \frac{6.674 \times 10^{-11} \times 5 \times 5}{(2)^2}$$
Step 3
Calculate the numerator
$$6.674 \times 10^{-11} \times 25 = 1.6685 \times 10^{-9}$$
Step 4
Calculate the denominator
$$r^2 = (2)^2 = 4 \text{ m}^2$$
Step 5
Divide to get the final answer
$$F = \frac{1.6685 \times 10^{-9}}{4} = 4.171 \times 10^{-10} \text{ N}$$
✅ Final Answer
$$\boxed{F \approx 4.17 \times 10^{-10} \text{ N}}$$
This is an extremely small force — which is why gravity between everyday objects is unnoticeable. Gravity only becomes significant when at least one object has a very large mass (like a planet).
💡 Key Insight — Inverse Square Law
Notice that r² appears in the denominator. This means:
  • If you double the distance → force becomes ¼ as strong
  • If you halve the distance → force becomes 4× stronger
This is called the Inverse Square Law.
